items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: before the quintet even, Buddy DeFranco, John Levy on bass, Denzil Best on drums and me

ctx.x: And Quincy too, yeah, he had charts by Quincy at that time. And we’d get in the audience and you’d be wet as I remember. You had your towel on, to listen to her in that group make music. Well there was a lot of things happening musically. You became very innovative though, with the Latin rhythms. You went through your Latin period there that was very exciting I thought.

That’s because before the quintet even, Buddy DeFranco, John Levy on bass, Denzil Best on drums and me, before the quintet, in the Clique Club in New York, opposite the Machito band, and when I start thinking about that, I could hear rhythmic complexity in that thing that was even ahead of some more simplified forms of jazz. Because in true African style, they would blend three or four rhythms together. A conga drum four and [scats]. And then the cowbell [scats].
